paper_metadata.title: TiAl/IN718 dissimilar brazing with TiZrNiCuCo high-entropy filler metal: phase characterization and fractography

evidence.quote: a novel high-entropy quinary amorphous TiZrNiCuCo filler alloy
a quinary amorphous high-entropy TiZrNiCuCo with a nominal composition of Ti34Zr26Ni18Cu15Co7 was fabricated and applied as the filler metal
Titanium and aluminum with high purity (99.97 and 99.7 wt%, respectively) were used for producing TiAl intermetallic compound.
The Ni-based IN718 superalloy was used in the solution treated standard heat treatment condition.

Alloying and casting in 2 × 10 × 30 mm mold were carried out in a vacuum arc remelting (VAR) furnace, and the ingot was remelted for 4 times.
The as-cast ingots were placed in the quartz capsule filled with the high purity (99.999%) Argon and inserted in the tube furnace and has been homogenized at 1100 °C for 24 h.

the ribbon-shaped filler metal was fabricated using a Melt Spin Furnace with a high speed rotating copper wheel (V = 1800 round per minute). The thickness of the obtained ribbons was 78 ± 4 μm.

evidence.section: 3.1.1 Reaction layer adjacent to the γ-TiAl

evidence.quote: led to the formation of a triple phase layer (spot C in Fig.3(a)) according to the ternary reaction (L+ τ2→τ1-Ti(Cu, Ni)2Al+τ3-Ti2(Cu, Ni)Al5)

evidence.section: 3.1.2 Diffusion zone adjacent to the IN718
evidence.quote: two distinct in situ Ni-based (γ) and Cr-based (αʹ) phases have precipitated in the solid-state γ-Ni matrix of the substrate (spot K)

evidence.section: 3.1.2 Diffusion zone adjacent to the IN718
evidence.quote: αʹ (Cr, Fe) and γ (Fe, Ni) have precipitated in the γ-Ni matrix of the IN718 substrate discontinuously

evidence.section: 3.1.2 Diffusion zone adjacent to the IN718

attributes.location: γ-Ni solid solution matrix of IN718 side; SZ near TiAl side

evidence.quote: A thin discontinuous phase zone (spot E) was detected in the TiAl side of the SZ that is considered a (Ti, Zr)2(Cu, Ni) single-phase zone.
isothermal solidification of a Zr-rich solid solution layer (spot H)
formed a continuous isothermal solidified layer which has enriched with Ti and Zr elements (spot D)
the excess amounts of them rejected and have been solidified as the (Ni, Cu)3(Ti, Zr) phase at the bonding temperature isothermally (spot I)
there is a thick TiNi single-phase solid solution mainly dissolved with Zr and Cu that solidified at the bonding temperature isothermally

attributes.location: adjacent to DZ of IN718 side

evidence.quote: the formation of a continuous Ti2Ni-based intermetallic compound which has been formed adjacent to the DZ of the IN718 side that is too brittle
The maximum shear strength of 396 MPa achieved at 1020 °C for 40-min bonding
the high temperature strength of the joint is 67% than that of the room temperature strength of the joint

the fracture behavior of the joints is brittle-dominated due to the presence of the brittle fracture appearances on the surfaces. Cleavage facets (CF) and cleavage planes (CP) were observed in the fracture surfaces as the cleavage fracture features.

the reduction of Cu and Ni and the increase of Ti alongside with Zr enrichment in the liquid phase led to an increase in melting temperature of the liquid phase. So, the remaining liquid started to solidify isothermally
intense dissolution of the TiAl and Ni-based IN718 substrates was occurred into the molten Ti-Zr-Ni-Cu-Co filler, and the diffusion of Al, Nb, Fe, Cr, and Ni
